key_insight: Thoracic aortic diameter and stiffness showed distinct circulating protein associations, suggesting different biological processes underlying these imaging traits.
clinical_relevance: These findings may inform future biomarker research for aortic remodelling but do not establish a screening test or treatment strategy.
method: Analysed 2,920 circulating proteins in 6,773 UK Biobank participants with plasma proteomics and cardiac imaging.
Used multivariable linear regression with false discovery rate correction.
Applied ranked-protein pathway enrichment and secondary principal component analysis.
evidence_signal: Fully adjusted models identified 417 proteins associated with aortic diameter and six with stiffness; the imaging traits were modestly correlated (r = 0.21).
watch_item: This is an observational aortic biology study, not AI cancer drug discovery; associations changed with adjustment and do not establish causality.
paper_title: Distinct circulating proteomic patterns associated with thoracic aortic diameter and stiffness: A proteome-wide study in the UK Biobank
